references.text: The Lord gave them rest from all their enemies around them, a parallel to the promise of rest fulfilled in Joshua.
The Lord's promise to give rest to the people, pointing forward to its fulfillment in the time of Joshua.
The promise that the Lord would deliver the enemies into Israel's hand, which is fulfilled here.
Direct connection with the preceding verse about the Lord giving Israel all the land he had promised their fathers.
Joshua refers back to this rest that the Lord gave Israel from all their enemies around them.
The promise that no one would be able to stand against Israel, which is fulfilled in this verse.
The Lord's promise to Joshua that no one would be able to stand against him, now confirmed as fulfilled here.
The Lord promises to deliver the enemies into Joshua's hand, a recurring theme that culminates in this verse.
The Lord's oath to Abraham to bless his descendants, which is fulfilled here.
The book of Hebrews reflects on how Joshua did not give them the final rest, pointing toward a greater rest in Christ.
